advances: Excludes universal support functions depending on direction only through the cap fraction by a fixed nonconstant C² transform.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Choose $\alpha\in(0,1)$ with $\phi'(\alpha)\ne0$. Apply stationary-cap-hessian-realization with $k=d-1$ and $A=-\operatorname{sign}(\phi'(\alpha))I_k$. This supplies a stationary direction $u$ at fraction $\alpha$ for which $\operatorname{Hess}_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}p_K(u)$ is a positive multiple of $A$, with arbitrarily large multiplier.

For any unit $w$ tangent to the sphere at $u$, convexity of the homogeneous extension of a support function $g$ requires that its second derivative on the line $u+\tau w$ be nonnegative at $\tau=0$. This extension on the line is $\sqrt{1+\tau^2}\,g(\cos(\arctan\tau)u+\sin(\arctan\tau)w)$, with second derivative $g(u)+\operatorname{Hess}_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}g(u)[w,w]$. At a stationary direction of $p_K$ with $g=\phi\circ p_K$, this equals $\phi(\alpha)+\phi'(\alpha)\operatorname{Hess}_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}p_K(u)[w,w]$ by the chain rule. It is negative for sufficiently large realization multiplier, contradicting the required convexity.
statement: For each $d\ge2$ and each nonconstant $\phi\in C^2((0,1))$, there is a convex polytope $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$ for which $u\mapsto\phi(p_K(u))$ on the unit sphere is not the support function of any convex body, where $p_K(u)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge0\}|/|K|$.
title: Scalar transforms of cap fraction cannot give universal support functions
